gloss: to have a bad experience; to suffer; to go through something unpleasant

definitions.gloss: to have a bad experience; to suffer; to go through something unpleasant
definitions.explanation: To experience something negative or unpleasant, often something one did not expect or deserve. Almost always used with a negative modifier describing the type of hardship.

examples.japanese: ひどい{目|め}に{遭|あ}った。
{旅行|りょこう}{先|さき}でとんでもない{目|め}に{遭|あ}った。
examples.english: I had an awful experience at my travel destination.

examples.japanese: {詐欺|さぎ}に{遭|あ}って、{散々|さんざん}な{目|め}に{遭|あ}った{人|ひと}の{話|はなし}を{聞|き}いて、{自分|じぶん}も{気|き}をつけようと{思|おも}った。
examples.english: After hearing the story of someone who was scammed and went through a terrible ordeal, I decided to be more careful myself.

notes:
The core expression is 〜{目|め}に{遭|あ}う, where {目|め} means "experience" and {遭|あ}う means "to encounter." It is almost exclusively used for negative experiences. The type of bad experience is specified by a modifier before {目|め}.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ひどい{目|め}に{遭|あ}う: to have a terrible experience
- {散々|さんざん}な{目|め}に{遭|あ}う: to go through a miserable ordeal
- とんでもない{目|め}に{遭|あ}う: to have an outrageous experience
- {怖|こわ}い{目|め}に{遭|あ}う: to have a frightening experience
- {痛|いた}い{目|め}に{遭|あ}う: to suffer painful consequences

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
- {目|め}に{遭|あ}わせる: to put someone through a bad experience — the causative form, meaning to inflict hardship on someone
- {被害|ひがい}に{遭|あ}う: to suffer damage; to be victimized — more formal, emphasizes concrete harm
- {苦労|くろう}する: to struggle; to have a hard time — emphasizes prolonged effort rather than a discrete bad event
